archetypes.name: design-implement-boundary
archetypes.rationale: The plan's core invariant is that design surfaces remain byte-identical while implement surfaces are stripped; no static reviewer specifically hunts for boundary leakage in shared scripts.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each shared script in scope (render-run-summary.sh, timing-report.sh, report-tokens Python modules), verify that the proposed conditionality—value-presence on --workflow-path and explicit LARCH_TIMING_SKILL=design gates—actually isolates design behavior from implement codepaths rather than relying on implicit fallback. Check that no design-only files (scripts/write-run-params.sh, scripts/read-workflow-path.sh, any skills/design/ path) appear in the modification list. Verify that the plan's claim of byte-identical design output is structurally guaranteed by the proposed conditionals, not merely asserted. Flag any proposed deletion or modification that could silently affect design runs even though the plan declares them out-of-scope. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: json-schema-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan promises JSON schema stability (workflow_path='unknown' in implement timing JSON and omission in report-tokens JSON appendix) for downstream consumers; this contract needs a dedicated reviewer.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the proposed awk/timing-report.sh changes preserve the JSON workflow_path key emitting 'unknown' for implement runs unconditionally—not just when no workflow row exists, but also when a legacy ledger has a v1 workflow row that will now be ignored. Check that the report-tokens Python JSON appendix omission for implement (plan: 'omits workflow for implement') is consistent with what the revised golden fixture expects and with RunRecord.workflow being retained as a field returning empty string. Confirm that no downstream code reading RunRecord.workflow treats empty string and None differently in ways the plan doesn't account for. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: md-script-pairing
archetypes.rationale: The plan modifies ~20 paired .sh/.md files; mismatches between shell behavior and doc updates are a silent drift risk not covered by the static panel.
archetypes.prompt_body: For every .sh script in the scope list that the plan proposes to modify, verify that a corresponding .md update is also proposed and that the described post-change behavior accurately matches the proposed .sh change—pay particular attention to flag tables, subcommand lists, and session-env tables in .md files whose .sh counterparts are losing keys or subcommands. Check that test spec .md files (test-step2-dispatch.md, test-timing-ledger.md, test-run-step5-review.md) describe the same test cases and assertions as their companion .sh harnesses after the proposed rewrites. Flag any .sh change that has no corresponding .md counterpart in the plan, or any .md update whose behavioral description diverges from the proposed .sh logic. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
